digests.title: AI 日报｜11月25日：MCP 配套技能与 Agent 工作流演进
digests.summary: MCP 服务可携带技能供 Claude Code 使用；ChatGPT Business 提供限时权益。[S4][S5] 本期还关注多 Agent 实践、历史研究案例及开放模型的全球采用讨论。[S1][S13][S10]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### MCP 服务可自带技能
Boris Cherny 表示，MCP 服务器现在可以随附自身的 skills，让 Claude Code 开箱即知如何使用这些服务。新增条目未提供配置方式、兼容范围或具体示例。[S4]

### ChatGPT Business 提供限时权益
Thibault Sottiaux 宣布，面向 ChatGPT Business 团队提供一次“banked reset”，以及截至 12 月 31 日不额外收费的 fast mode。原帖未解释重置机制、额度及具体适用条件，不宜据此理解为无限量使用。[S5]

## Builder 动态

- **Antigravity 多 Agent 实践教程**：Peter Yang 分享了一门免费、17 分钟的视频课程，介绍 Gemini 4 Neon 与 Antigravity 的组合。他称 Orchestrator 和 `/swarm` 适合多 Agent 规划与构建，曾同时运行 42 个 Agent；`/grill-me` 可通过追问澄清需求。有关远程控制优于 Claude Code 的说法属于其个人体验，并非独立评测结论。[S1]
- **把编程 Agent 做成可嵌入内核**：Guillermo Rauch 解释，其提及工具采用 CLI，是因为它只是 `libfx` 的薄封装；目标是构建尽可能小且智能的编程 Agent 内核，嵌入浏览器、服务器、移动端和桌面等环境。这是设计目标，条目没有证明这些平台均已得到支持。[S8]
- **OC 的维护重心转向可靠性**：Peter Steinberger 表示，OC 已在专业消费者和企业采用中找到定位，近期主要投入速度、可靠性与安全性，同时提及新记忆系统及即将到来的 OpenClaw ID。他也强调了维护可靠、免费开源软件的工作量与情绪压力。采用情况与功能评价均为作者自述，未附量化数据。[S12]

## 值得阅读

### 历史研究中的“提出线索—档案核验”案例
Simon Willison 转述历史学教授 Mark Humphries 的案例：GPT-6.2 Astra 据称在 22 分钟内，为耶鲁大学 Beinecke 图书馆收藏的一本匿名 1808 年素描册识别作者，并提出一份纸质档案来源作为验证线索；据该案例叙述，后续查验支持了其假设。[S13]

**阅读价值**在于模型不仅给出归属判断，还指向可进一步核查的史料。不过，这仍是单个案例报告，不能据此推断模型处理历史归属问题的普遍准确率；现有摘录也不足以复核完整证据链。[S13]

### 编程 Agent 何时开始真正省时间？
Willison 在《十二个月里的三个 LLM 拐点》中回顾自己的使用变化：他认为，Claude Opus 4.5 让 Claude Code 从需要频繁纠正的工具，变成处理多数日常编程问题时能够带来明确提速的助手。这是个人经验判断，不是统一基准测试。[S14]

所给摘录只展开了文章开头，无法据此完整概括标题中的三个拐点。[S14]

## 观察

- **Token 需求可能随 Agent 工作方式阶梯式增长**：Amjad Masad 提出，从自动补全、聊天到 Agent、长时自主 Agent 和群体协作，每次工具框架创新都会打开更大的潜在消耗空间，但用户找到实际用途存在滞后。这是一种需求增长假说，条目未提供用量或收入数据验证。[S3]
- **开放模型竞争也关乎部署控制权**：Masad 认为，各国对本土基础设施和自主控制的需求，会影响模型、芯片及技术栈的全球采用；开放模型因此具有战略意义。这篇观点帖适合用来观察“前沿能力”之外的竞争维度，但不能当作各国采购趋势已被证实的结论。[S10]

digests.title: AI 日报｜Claude 整合插件生态，GLM-5.4 采用循环 Transformer
digests.summary: Claude 推进插件整合、交付工具与企业安全能力；GLM-5.4 采用循环 Transformer，但据资料尚未开放权重；Datasette 打通对话制图与面板状态联动。[S6][S7][S8][S14][S16]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### Claude：连接器与技能合并为插件

Claude 官方宣布将 connectors 与 skills 统一为 plugins，用于连接工具、扩展技能，或同时完成两者。插件已面向 Free、Pro、Max、Ultra 套餐开放，Team 与 Enterprise 将随后支持；官方称可浏览的插件超过 10,000 个。这里的数量是官方披露的目录规模，不代表插件质量或使用量。[S8]

企业端另有两项更新：
- **Claude Ship 测试版**：11 月 23 日宣布面向 Team 和 Enterprise 推出。发布者将其定位于改善代码生成之后的 PR 交付环节，但本次材料未披露具体功能、权限边界或效果数据。[S7]
- **零数据保留与安全防护结合**：支持零数据保留（ZDR）的 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS）面向符合条件的企业进入公开测试。官方称，该机制可跨多次请求识别滥用，同时兼容 ZDR，并与超过 100 家客户共同开发；具体实现方式未在所给材料中展开。[S6]

### GLM-5.4：以循环层增加计算深度

据 Simon Willison 的介绍，Z.ai 的 GLM-5.4 已可使用，是该实验室首个采用循环 Transformer 架构的模型：让一组共享权重的层迭代运行，以不增加参数量的方式加深计算。**这说明了架构思路，并不直接证明性能优于其他模型**；本次材料没有提供可比较的评测结果。[S14]

接入方面，作者测试时需订阅 Coding Plan，普通 API 暂不能访问该模型；Coding Plan 密钥可通过 OpenAI 兼容的 Responses API 使用。文章同时指出，GLM-5.4 当时尚未开放权重，因此不宜将其归为开源模型发布。[S14]

## Builder 动态

### Datasette：对话生成图表，并跟随用户操作更新上下文

11 月 24 日发布的 **datasette-charts 0.2a0** 接入 Datasette Agent：用户可在聊天中指定数据表并要求制图，图表既能内嵌展示，也能在侧边面板的图表构建器中打开。演示中，用户在面板切换数据后，Agent 能在后续问答中识别并解释新的图表内容。[S16]

配套的 **datasette-agent 0.7a1** 改进了 iframe 侧边面板的 URL 片段导航，以便与通过 fragment hash 表达交互状态的插件更深入地集成，并修复图表插件相关问题。这组更新的看点不只是“聊天生成图表”，而是对话与可视化界面之间的状态衔接。[S15][S16]

### OpenAI 内部使用 dots 构建 dots

OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 表示，dots 正迅速成为内部完成工作的主要方式之一，且已有 dots 参与构建 dots 系统本身。这是一则内部使用情况的陈述；材料没有解释其完整产品形态、开放范围，也没有量化生产力收益。[S5]

## 观察

### 个性化模型评估值得借鉴，但不能外推为通用排名

Guillermo Rauch 称，他让 Fable 分析自己的编程会话，在 Opus 与 Gemini Neon 之间做选择，结果选中了 Neon。这提供了一个实用思路：以个人真实工作记录作为选型依据。但材料未给出评分标准、样本范围或复现实验，因此结果只能视为其个人工作流下的评估，不能据此判定模型整体优劣。[S2]

### ChatGPT 质量提升仍需等待实际验证

Sottiaux 预告，相关更新逐步推送后，用户应能感到 ChatGPT 回答质量显著提升，并提及简化应用、提速及融合聊天与工作的投入。这属于产品方向与效果预期；本次材料没有给出具体模型版本、完整上线时间或评测数据，不宜写成已向所有用户兑现的改进。[S9]

digests.title: AI 日报：视频剪辑自动化与 CI/CD Agent
digests.summary: 本次新增关注 AutoClip 的长视频再利用流程、OpenSRE 的 CI/CD 可靠性定位，以及借助 Claude 制作表单样式对照页的实践。项目均未提供发布时间，不视为今日发布。[S1][S4][S5]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### AutoClip：从长视频到短视频发布素材

AutoClip 是一款开源 AI 视频剪辑桌面工具。项目介绍称，输入链接后，可将播客、访谈、课程等长视频自动剪成短视频，并生成字幕、封面和发布文案，面向抖音、小红书、TikTok、Reels 与 YouTube Shorts 等平台。[S4]

值得关注的是，它的功能范围不止剪辑，还覆盖内容再利用与发布素材准备。不过，现有资料仅为项目简介，无法确认剪辑质量、平台适配效果或实际使用成本。[S4]

## Builder 动态

### OpenSRE：面向 CI/CD 可靠性的开源 Agent

OpenSRE 将自身定位为服务于 CI/CD 可靠性的开源 Agent。新增资料未说明其具体任务、集成方式或自主执行边界，因此目前适合作为工程自动化方向的观察项目，尚不足以判断落地能力。[S1]

## 值得阅读

### 用 Claude 构建 HTML 下拉框样式对照页

Simon Willison 在 11 月 22 日的文章中记录：由于不满意 HTML `<select>` 在不同浏览器中的默认外观，他让 Claude Fable 5.2 制作展示多种样式方案的页面，并计划在桌面与移动浏览器中截图比较。[S5]

经过实验，他偏好的方案使用 `appearance: none` 移除原生外观，再配置边框、内边距与 SVG 背景箭头。这提供了一个具体的 AI 辅助前端工作流：先生成可比较的样例，再通过浏览器检查选择方案；不能据此认定所有浏览器的兼容性已获验证。[S5]

## 观察

本次新增项目中，AutoClip 指向内容生产自动化，OpenSRE 指向工程可靠性自动化，体现了两种不同的 Agent／AI 工具应用方向；仅凭这两条简介，不能推断行业整体趋势。[S1][S4]

上述两个 GitHub 项目均未提供发布时间，本期仅作新增收录，不将其表述为今日创建或发布。[S1][S4]

digests.title: AI 日报｜黎曼猜想证明声明待核验，Agent 工具链持续细化
digests.summary: 黎曼猜想相关证明声明引发人机协作讨论，但所给材料未证明其获独立确认；ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代，Agent 技能与插件工具增多，Token 滥用暴露产品成本风险。[S28][S11][S13][S17][S26]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### 黎曼猜想相关声明引发关注，不能等同于已确认突破
- **当事人声明**：Simon Willison 摘引 Levent Alpöge 的文字称，后者相信自己与 Claude 找到了黎曼猜想的证明，方法还可扩展至广义黎曼猜想，并称已完成不依赖额外假设的形式化论证。这是被转引的自述，不是材料所能独立确认的数学结论。[S28]
- **另一条研究线索**：Ravi Vakil 的引文介绍，Alessandro Masullo 也有广义黎曼猜想的候选证明，Brian Conrad 已持续审阅数月并提供反馈；该工作被明确描述为未使用 AI。引文仍将其称为候选证明，而非已获最终确认的成果。[S29]
- **编辑判断**：讨论应区分“提出证明”“形式化声明”与“获得独立核验”。现有材料不足以确认上述证明成立，也不足以判断两项工作的关系。社交平台已出现将其称为“突破”的评论，报道不宜直接沿用这一确定性表述。[S7][S28][S29]

### Token 滥用正在影响 AI 产品的试用策略
据 Simon Willison 对 Claire Vo 视频的介绍，ChatPRD 遭遇反复注册免费试用、套用促销码，以及借其 Agent 获取算力或开展其他商业活动的滥用；Claire 正逐步取消免费试用。对 Builder 而言，这个案例提示：试用额度不仅是获客成本，也可能成为被转售或挪用的资源。材料未提供损失规模。[S26]

## Builder 动态

- **ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代**：11 月 22 日的帖子称，团队已在准备下一次较大更新，并就前一天的桌面应用更新征集反馈。现有信息没有列出已上线功能或下一版发布时间，不宜据此扩写更新清单。[S11]
- **Muru：AI 辅助开发 Python 应用服务器**：据介绍，mod_wsgi 发起者 Graham Dumpleton 正使用 AI 辅助构建 Rust 服务器 Muru，目标是支持 ASGI、WSGI 应用的开发与生产运行。他持续公开架构和开发过程，涉及 worker、发布、容器、扩缩容及追踪等主题；材料未提供性能对比或成熟度验证。[S30]
- **Amuse 宣布开源**：Amjad Masad 发帖称，由 Replit Missions 构建的 Amuse 已开源。所给文本没有项目功能、许可证或部署方式，暂只能确认这项开源声明。[S9]

## 开源趋势

以下依据仓库简介整理；所给材料没有 Star 增量、下载量或使用数据，因此不能据此判断热度排名。

| 方向 | 项目与具体看点 |
| --- | --- |
| 安全技能 | **Claude-BugHunter**：简介列出 82 项技能、15 个斜杠命令，以及覆盖 24 类核心漏洞的 681 个已披露报告模式，面向漏洞挖掘与外部红队工作。[S13] |
| 开发方法与扩展 | **superpowers** 自述为 Agent 技能框架与软件开发方法；**cursor/plugins** 提供 Cursor 插件规范及官方插件。[S14][S17] |
| 软件接口 Agent 化 | **CLI-Anything** 以让软件具备面向 Agent 的命令行接口为目标；这是项目定位，不能理解为已适配所有软件。[S15] |
| 跨工具技能 | **stitch-skills** 面向 Stitch MCP server，简介称遵循 Agent Skills 开放标准，适配多种编码 Agent。[S23] |
| 数据接入 | **Firecrawl** 将搜索、抓取和数据访问整合到一个 API，简介称可访问 550 多个数据提供方；实际覆盖与服务条件未在材料中展开。[S18] |
| 垂直工作流 | **diagram-design** 提供 45 类图表的 HTML、SVG 设计能力；**app-store-compliance** 将商店拒审模式、隐私检查和提交前检查整理为手册与 Agent 技能。[S21][S24] |

**趋势判断**：这批项目的共同方向，是把开发方法、工具接口和领域检查项封装成 Agent 可调用的组件，而不只是发布独立聊天产品。这是对本批样本的归纳，不代表整个开源生态的统计结论。[S13][S14][S15][S23][S24]

## 值得阅读

1. **Muru 开发记录：经验如何参与 AI 编程。** 摘录强调，即使 AI 承担大量表层工作，判断“哪里还不够好”仍依赖开发者积累。适合关注 AI 辅助工程实践、而非只看生成速度的读者。[S30]
2. **PostgreSQL 19 的 `WAIT FOR LSN`。** 11 月 19 日的文章介绍，通过等待备库回放到指定日志位置，让后续查询读到此前在主库完成的写入；还说明了可选超时的行为。这是早于本期主要动态的工程阅读补充。[S25]
3. **llm-gemini 0.38.1：推理档位与成本。** 作者称此次修复补上部分模型的 `xhigh` 设置；其示例中，同一模型从 `high` 切换至 `xhigh` 后，输出 Token 从 5,311 增至 31,477，费用从 3.99 美分增至 23.61 美分。这只是单个示例，不足以证明更高档位对所有任务都更划算。[S27]

## 观察

- **人机协作能力仍值得单独评估。** trq212 的连续帖子认为，与模型合作推动前沿本身就是技术能力，并表示尚未看到这项能力的收益递减。这是作者观点；它与 Muru 开发记录中强调人的质量判断相呼应，但不能替代生产率实测。[S4][S5][S6][S30]
- **多 Agent 协作出现可跟踪的组织线索。** Amjad Masad 转述一名高中生尝试让 GTA6 在 PC 上运行，并强调通过 GitHub Issues 协调 Agent 群。值得继续观察的是任务拆分与验收机制；材料没有代码、演示或独立验证，不能确认移植进度与效果。[S12]
- **供应商数据回传疑问尚缺证据。** swyx 发帖质疑某些提供方是否在秘密回传数据，但文本没有指明提供方、回传内容或技术证据。目前只能记录为待核实质疑，不能据此认定存在隐私违规。[S1]

items.title: America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return mat
items.excerpt:
America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl

items.excerpt: GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook . Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work. Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue ? Mark thinks it will be mild: But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. items.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
items.excerpt: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months. Here's the video of the talk. In this post I'm going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply. Coding agents in November 2025 Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5 . With hindsight, this was a consequential model. In the Opus 4.5 announcement, Anthropic said: Testers noted that Claude Opus 4.5 handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding. They told us that, when pointed at a complex, multi-system bug, Opus 4.5 figures out the fix. They said that tasks that were near-impossible for Sonnet 4.5 just a few weeks ago are now within reach. This held up. Claude Code was 9 months old at that point, having been introduced alongside Claude 3.7 Sonnet on February 24th, 2025. Opus 4.5 was the first model I had used with Claude Code where the default result was generally the right thing. I hadn't been using Claude Code as a daily driver because it didn't feel reliable enough - I had to correct it often enough that it didn't feel like a clear accelerant. The new Opus changed that. For most of the coding problems I faced on a daily basis, Opus would get them right . It was clearly faster than working through the problems myself. Also in November, OpenAI released GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, GPT-5.1-Codex, and GPT-5.1-Codex-Max. These had a similar effect on their Codex coding agent: it became reliably useful for many of my coding tasks. The timing was convenient, because the December holidays were upon us. items.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
items.excerpt:
Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should. items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.excerpt: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API. It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model. I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! items.title: This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math
items.excerpt:
This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math. We’re entering an era where solving problems will look very different from how we solved them in the past.

“This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.”

It used to be the case that to solve a particular problem - code, life sciences, math, cyber, engineering, and so on - you were ultimately bound by how much information an individual or team could retain and understand about the space. More information or more team members don’t always help, because it gets harder to connect the dots or coordinate amongst everyone. AI changes that completely. 

For the first time ever we can decouple the human context limits and ability to work through information from our ability to drive productivity or discoveries. This is likely not just a small increase in the kinds of discoveries we can drive, but a qualitative shift in human output. 

Now every single form of prior art, insight, past research, past decision, or unrelated breakthrough, can be used for the discovery or creation of something new. This is useful for anything from cybersecurity to life sciences research. Agents will be able to correlate entirely unrelated work to a separate project; scan every bit of data in your enterprise for solving a problem; and so on. 

The solutions may not be as elegant

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.excerpt: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse

items.title: llm-gemini 0.38.1
items.excerpt: Release: llm-gemini 0.38.1 Gemini 4 Carbon only supports low , medium and high reasoning levels - but Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon both have an extra xhigh level. I missed that when I added those models to the llm-gemini plugin, which is now fixed in this dot release. The xhigh setting for Hydrogen makes a significant difference. I updated my Gemini 4 comparison grid - note how Hydrogen at high used 5,311 output tokens and cost 3.99 cents, but the same model at xhigh used 31,477 output tokens, cost 23.61 cents, and produced a pelican that's competitive with Gemini 4 Neon: Tags: gemini , llm , llm-reasoning , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai , llms , google , generative-ai

items.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
items.excerpt: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...] Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. — Levent Alpöge , alpo.ge/remark.pdf Tags: anthropic , claude , generative-ai , mathematics , ai , llms , levent-alpoge

items.title: Muru
items.excerpt: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar 2026-11-22 — Muru: when lazy imports help That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Tags: graham-dum
